clause.quote: Given a local or remote event, a non-controller, non-witness, non-delegator validator MUST first verify the event's controller signatures, witness signatures (if witnessed), and delegator anchoring seal (if delegated) before it can accept that event into its copy of that event's KEL.

inferred_from.inference: The sentence states what a validator must verify before it can accept an event, not that it must accept one that passes. No sentence obliges a validator to accept anything, so that a validator should accept an event that passes every check, and that the event is then on the trunk, is inferred and graded SHOULD (docs/design.md, KERI, What MUST means here).

description: An inception, then a rotation whose configuration traits are [DID], signed by the exposed next key. DID may appear only in an inception (lines 367 and 373), so a validator must drop the rotation (line 367), and the key state stays the inception's.

dispute.raised_at: generators/DISAGREEMENTS.md in this repository, 2026-10-15; not yet raised with keripy or the KERI specification working group.
dispute.summary: keripy main reads configuration traits only from an identifier's inception (Kever.config is called when the Kever is created, never from Kever.update), so it accepts a rotation that carries EO, DND or DID as if its traits were empty, applies the rotation to the key state, and treats a later event at the rotation's sequence number as duplicitous.
